key_insight: Differentiable foundation models enable joint optimization of crystal composition and structure toward target properties, including band gaps suited to solar absorbers.
engineering_relevance: This approach could accelerate photovoltaic materials screening by designing crystals toward a 1.34 eV band gap while penalizing energetic instability.
method: DEFEAT extends pretrained EquiformerV3 to continuous species weights and site occupancies without fractional-data retraining.
Property-model gradients and a learned energy penalty jointly optimize composition, atom count, positions, and lattice vectors.
Validate candidates with first-principles calculations and assess finite-temperature phase competition using machine-learned potentials.
evidence_signal: SCAN calculations confirm ten novel crystal structures with gaps within 20% of the 1.34 eV target on their respective raw or empirically corrected scales, all within 70 meV/atom of the DFT hull.
watch_item: Training-functional band-gap bias propagates into designs unless corrected in the objective; the reported calculations do not establish solar-cell efficiency or experimental synthesizability.
paper_title: Inverse design of superconductors and semiconductors with differentiable foundation models
